subject: Multi-entity PO handoff — portal vs email envelope
messages:
From: Claire Rowe <ap@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying multi-entity PO submission — portal vs email

Hi Vanessa / Jordan,

We’re finishing up vendor setup but ran into a snag: several of our POs for Redwood are issued at the subsidiary level (billing_entity = "NorthBridge Services, Inc.") while the portal appears to accept a single legal entity per supplier profile. Our AP team has two questions before we finalize:

1) Can your portal accept an "envelope" or multi-entity PO payload (one submission with a billing_entity column per line)?
2) If the portal can’t, can we fall back to an email envelope workflow and what subject token / header do you need so invoices land in the right ledger?

I attached a sanitized invoice (compact-invoice-sample.csv) and a PDF of the offending PO (po-multiline-example.pdf) so you can see the fields. We’d prefer to use the portal long-term but need a reliable email fallback for this account during onboarding.

Thanks — appreciate any guidance/constraints.

Best,
Claire Rowe
Director, Accounts Payable
NorthBridge Health
attachments: compact-invoice-sample.csv, po-multiline-example.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Claire Rowe <ap@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying multi-entity PO submission — portal vs email

Hi Claire — thanks for the examples, very helpful. Short answers up front:

- Portal: our hosted portal currently expects a single primary billing_entity per supplier profile; it does not accept per-line billing_entity values today. That said, we can onboard NorthBridge with the account-level billing entity set to your preferred remit entity and map alternate entities via a secondary mapping (manual step during onboarding).

- Email envelope fallback: yes, we support an email-backstop envelope that includes a subject token we can route on. If you use the format NBH-AP|PO:<PO_NUMBER>|BILL:<billing_entity_code> in the subject we’ll route and autopopulate the billing_entity field during ingestion. Example subject: NBH-AP|PO:548231|BILL:NBSI

To move forward I’ve attached our vendor onboarding form (vendor-onboarding-form.pdf) — please complete the billing_entity mapping table on page 2. If you prefer to continue with portal-only we’ll need one of the following: (a) migrate POs to the primary entity before upload, or (b) we perform a short-lived manual mapping during onboarding (2–3 business days).

Next steps I suggest:
- Claire: fill the onboarding form and return (we’ll use that to seed the mapping).
- Jordan: can you confirm whether Finance is comfortable with the subject token approach and if we should require DocuSign for the mapping table?

I’ll schedule a 30-min call if that helps.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

attachments: vendor-onboarding-form.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: internal: NBH multi-entity PO — email fallback proposal

Jordan / Marissa,

Looping you in on NorthBridge (NBH) onboarding. They sent example POs that include multiple billing entities per PO. My proposed path:

1) Primary approach: portal onboarding with account set to the majority remit entity. We run a one-time mapping for any legacy POs during onboarding (manual reconciliation by Ops).
2) Fallback: enable email-envelope ingestion for the first 30 days, routing invoices that match the subject token NBH-AP|PO:<PO>|BILL:<entity>. Envelope ingestion will parse the CSV and set billing_entity per-line.

Questions / decision points:
- Legal: do we want the billing_entity mapping form to be signed (DocuSign) for audit trail? If yes, we should include Legal and ask for standard clause.
- Finance: what SLAs for manual mapping (T+2 business days?) — need confirmation.

If you’re okay, I’ll confirm the subject token and provide Claire the completed onboarding form template. I’m recommending we flag this as "email fallback allowed" in the onboarding record so the client can go live while portal improvements are queued.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Claire Rowe <ap@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying multi-entity PO submission — portal vs email

Thanks Vanessa — that works. We will:

- Complete the vendor onboarding form (attached) and include the billing_entity codes.
- Use the subject token format NBH-AP|PO:548231|BILL:NBSI when sending email fallback invoices.
- Send a short CSV sample (attached) with the per-line billing_entity column for you to validate ingestion.

Two quick follow-ups:
1) PO stamping: do you stamp incoming PDFs with the PO on ingestion or do you require the vendor to preserve PO as filename/subject?
2) Credits/adjustments: when an invoice line is split across two entities, how do you prefer we structure the line items (two lines vs one line with split amounts)?

If you can confirm PO stamping and preferred split-line formatting, we’ll finalize the form and flip the switch on the email fallback.

Appreciate the quick turn — Claire
Claire Rowe
Director, Accounts Payable
NorthBridge Health
